definitions: To unfairly change the rules or criteria of a process or competition while it is in progress.
To alter the conditions or requirements of an agreement or task after they have already been established, making it more difficult to achieve the original objective.
examples: They kept shifting the goalpost, so we never knew what was expected.
It feels like the company is shifting the goalpost on our performance metrics.
You can't just shift the goalpost in the middle of the project.
